title: More room for the model, stage 2: exact fixes to the lead agent's rules
request: The owner approved stage 2 of the plan: close the lead agent's dead ends, read a build's yes in code, accept true quotes, record several facts at once, keep working notes out of the message, make the number check cut a line instead of a list, and let the team walk run a project it cannot map. The safety rules stay.
spec: Each row of the stage's table gets a test. A build still needs the person's yes, the outcome is still never guessed, and a number nobody gave never reaches the person. One test proves that in every state it tries, a move that decides what the person gets is open.
plan: fix the yes to a build, the dead ends, the options and the second reading
fix the quote rule in the core, notes in a list, the reply's assembly, the number check's unit and the team walk
extract what a turn does on hearing a message, so tests start from real states
write a test per row and the way-forward test
rerun the harness suites, review, measure

decisions.decision: Code reads the yes to a build from the person's latest message; the quote is optional
decisions.why: the rule is that a build needs their yes, not that the model copies it word for word

decisions.decision: A go-ahead opens the options, not a start
decisions.why: the person keeps the choice; what is open is stated as assumptions

decisions.decision: Only a message that is nothing but a go-ahead answers a question about building
decisions.why: the review showed a go-ahead about something else was read as a yes to build

decisions.decision: Readiness is unchanged: an assumption still does not count as known
decisions.why: that rule is deliberate and measured by the exam; notes in a list remove the cost instead

decisions.decision: A leading yes with a condition still counts as a yes
decisions.why: an earlier decision of the owner made it so; the reviewer disagrees and it is reported as open

change: The lead agent's start, propose, ask, note and build tools, the number check, the reply's assembly and the second reading; the core's quote rule; the team walk's fallback to the stage path; the trace reader's names for refusals; a test file for the stage.

findings.defect: A go-ahead about something else was read as a yes to building.
findings.scenario: The agent asked whether to build or first show a rate; the person asked for the rate; a build was recorded.
findings.fix: Only a message that is nothing but a go-ahead counts, and only after a question whose own sentence names the build.

findings.defect: The team walk's fallback could not pass the person's approval.
findings.scenario: The first walk ran its stages; the walk after the approval was refused as existing work.
findings.fix: A project that walked its stages directly keeps doing so; it is recorded in the workspace.

findings.defect: A new refusal name was read before an older, more exact one.
findings.scenario: A closed-list refusal was counted as a bad argument and a test failed.
findings.fix: The new names come after the closed-list ones.

findings.defect: A go-ahead skipped a doubt about the kind of work that had never been told.
findings.scenario: A report was asked for, the person said go ahead, and a prediction started with no word of their request.
findings.fix: A go-ahead skips only a doubt already told for that move.

findings.defect: An option could leave the person's own pick by naming another kind of work.
findings.scenario: The kind of work was derived from the tool after the pick was checked.

findings.defect: A short real answer beside the options was dropped as a working note.
findings.scenario: The person got the fallback line under the options.
findings.fix: Only short notes beside bookkeeping calls are dropped, and a turn's only words always stay.

findings.defect: One option passing the checks led to two refusals each way.
findings.scenario: No table, a go-ahead: the options were refused for want of a second, and the start as not ready.
findings.fix: The one option that passed may be started after a go-ahead, in that turn only.

findings.defect: A leading yes with a condition still counts as a yes to building.
findings.scenario: A yes that waits for someone else's approval records a build.
findings.fix: Not changed: an earlier owner decision; reported as open.

measurements.name: The gate on the lead agent after stages one and two
measurements.gate: hab_gate_v1, pinned before the repair: every check must hold
measurements.result: not passed for either model or set of people; no dead end, no fallback line, no made-up number and no build without a yes in any lead-agent conversation; on the people the repair was not tuned on, no score moved outside noise
measurements.next: stage four: think first, choose the kind of work last
limits: few written people, each played once; the judge is a model
the repair was tuned on the first set

outcome: The lead agent no longer gets stuck, refuses a real yes, or drops a list for one number. It still plans below the same model alone, and on new people its scores did not move.
lessons: A rule that reads intent from words must be tested on words that mean something else.
Gains measured on the cases watched during a fix must be checked on cases nobody watched.
risks: Reading the yes in code could accept a yes that was not about building.
